title: Stalk localization for derived internal Hom of a coherent sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], let $\mathcal G$ be any $\mathcal O_X$-module, let $x\in X$, and let $i\in\mathbf Z$. Then $\mathcal H^i(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F[0],\mathcal G[0]))_x$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] is canonically isomorphic to $H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x[0],\mathcal G_x[0]))$. Here $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}$ is the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-point ringed site with structure ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and $H^i$ is the cohomology in its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Lemma lemma-stalk-internal-hom (Tag 0GM8), case (2), together with perfect.tex Lemma lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian (Tag 08E8)

proof.text: The question is local at $x$: for an open $U\ni x$, [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open] gives $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F[0],\mathcal G[0])|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F|_U[0],\mathcal G|_U[0])$, and restriction to $U$ commutes with cohomology sheaves and does not change stalks at $x$. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with $A$ Noetherian. The coherent sheaf $\mathcal F|_U$ is $\widetilde M$ for a finite $A$-module $M$, and [lem-sc-coherent-affine-free-resolution] supplies a bounded-above complex $E^\bullet$ of finite-rank free $\mathcal O_U$-modules and a quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to\mathcal F|_U[0]$.

source.place: Lemma 01XZ (coherent-lemma-coherent-Noetherian), with Algebra 00LP and the affine quasi-coherent equivalence

proof.text: Because $E^\bullet$ is bounded above and termwise finite free, and $\mathcal G|_U[0]$ is bounded below, the bounded-above locally free Hom calculation identifies the total complex $\mathcal H om^\bullet_{\mathcal O_U}(E^\bullet,\mathcal G|_U[0])$ with a representative of $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F|_U[0],\mathcal G|_U[0])$.

source.place: derived internal Hom from bounded-above locally free complexes; Lemma 0GM8 case (2)

proof.text: For each degree, finite freeness gives $\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E^n,\mathcal G|_U)_x\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(E^n_x,\mathcal G_x)$, and these identifications commute with the differentials. Thus the stalk of the displayed Hom complex is $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(E^\bullet_x,\mathcal G_x[0])$.

source.place: Lemma 0GM8 case (2), stalks of Hom for finite locally free terms

proof.text: Stalks are exact, so $E^\bullet_x\to\mathcal F_x[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism; each $E^n_x$ is finite free, hence projective, over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Therefore the complex in Step 3 is a projective resolution model of the local derived Hom.

source.place: Lemma 0GM8 case (2), exactness of stalks; derived-categories projective-resolution computation

proof.text: Taking cohomology in degree $i$: since stalks are exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], the stalk at $x$ of $\mathcal H^i$ of the complex of Step 2 is $H^i$ of its stalk complex, which by Steps 3--4 is $H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x[0],\mathcal G_x[0]))$; with Step 1 this yields $\mathcal H^i(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F[0],\mathcal G[0]))_x\cong H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x[0],\mathcal G_x[0]))$. The construction is canonical because the stalk and derived-Hom comparison maps are natural.
